combatants._comment: Riverfarm's own ally, `river_wolf_pack`/`briar_collectors`/`briar_collectors_deep` roster (issue #10/#11 FIX-FIRST: Relc has no fictional basis at Riverfarm -- reached solely via a SOLO Door arrival, Liscor's own Watch guardsman, no come-along beat, no locality; see wi-adding-an-encounter's ally precedent). CANON-GROUNDED, ORIGINAL+flag (docs/design/character-profiles-staging.md): wiki.wanderinginn.com/Riverfarm attests a [Hunter] class among the village's defenders (Califfy, Thel Grasse) -- this combatant realizes that attested profession, not an invented one. Stats/weapon_die/ai/skills are an EXACT clone of `relc`'s block (same numbers, only id/display_name/sprite differ) -- R2/R3's tuned harness bands (sim_combat_batch.gd RIVERFARM_CELLS, gated 0.55-0.95/0.55-0.85, measured 0.84) were tuned against this exact stat block under the old id; changing any stat here invalidates them. No `combat_scale` override (unlike relc's 0.61, which contains his bespoke 124px Drake frame) -- the `a_hunter` sprite is a plain 64px human frame, same convention as every other human-sized combatant. Fields only when `hunter_will_come` is banked (data/dialogue/riverfarm_hunter.json's own come-along beat, at the village) -- never on `met_relc` alone.

Canon Liscor-area ambush predator (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Shield_Spiders -- black-and-silver armored carapace, Silver-rank individually, nest under Liscor's Dungeon). A goblin_raider-class melee reskin nudged toward the carapace fantasy: +con (armored back), +dex (ambusher), lower int/cha. SPRITE STAND-IN: uses `bat` (the only dark cave-creature sheet in-tree) -- flagged in docs/VISUAL-LOG.md for a real arachnid sprite (Track B / PixelLab). str/weapon_die tuned down from an earlier reading: the nest's ['shield_spider','shield_spider'] roster now correctly fields TWO distinct combatants (WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id rosters at build time) instead of silently collapsing to one, so `cisterns_fight`'s warrior-L1-SOLO clear is a genuine 2-spider fight -- these numbers keep that findable (real risk, not free) without trivializing the ally-backed/level-2 approaches. Balance is MEASURED-only in sim_combat_batch.gd's ENCOUNTER_CELLS (see report).

The sewers' weak trash pack. Wiki lacks a named sewer-rat monster, so realized SPRITE-HONESTLY as cave bats (`bat` sheet, same as cave_spider's 'Cave Bat') -- canon-plausible tunnel vermin, flagged generic-diegetic per the spec. Deliberately fragile (low con/weapon_die) so the sewers_walkthrough autoplay clears it fast.

Raskghar scout -- canon nocturnal cave predator (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Raskghar): a cross between an upright bear and a lion, towers over Gnolls, tracks and ambushes prey. A bruiser-class melee pair: still tougher than a goblin_raider (con/weapon_die), low int/cha. Serves DOUBLE duty -- the deep_tunnels route-fight pair AND the 2 scout adds in the Awakened's boss roster (its ['raskghar_scout','raskghar_scout'] entry now correctly fields TWO distinct combatants -- WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id rosters at build time). str/con/weapon_die are tuned so the FULL two-scout add plus the boss holds awakened_boss_w2_relc's 0.6-0.75 band as a real 3-vs-2 fight; the route-fight cells (measured-only, no band) read easier at these numbers, which is fine. combat_scale 0.4492 contains the hulking 124px frame at the feet (the Relc containment lesson); sprite is a real directional PixelLab v2 idle/walk/slice set. Balance MEASURED-only in sim_combat_batch.gd SCOUT_CELLS; GATED via BOSS_CELLS (see raskghar_awakened's own comment).

The Awakened Raskghar BOSS -- canon (a Raskghar that ate a Gnoll's heart, permanently smarter, matches a Level-20 warrior). High-HP bruiser. Its signature [Raskghar Maul] is a reaching slowed-rider swing on the EXISTING spell_damage+applies machinery (NO new effect type). `ai: caster` is REQUIRED, not decorative: the melee AI only fires attack/power_strike by name, so a `caster` boss (leads with the range-2 maul, falls through to claws) is the only shipped profile that actually LANDS the slow without a combat_ai.gd change. combat_scale 0.4839 lets it loom ~2 cells while HP bars stay readable. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd BOSS_CELLS -- GATED 0.6-0.75 vs warrior2+Relc, measured solo. The boss ENCOUNTER entity (party/veto beat) is separate from this combatant + arena + harness band. weapon_die is tuned alongside raskghar_scout's own stats (see that record's comment) -- both levers hold the 0.6-0.75 band against the boss's FULL two-scout add (a genuine 3-vs-2 fight).

The rift_vermin_leak trash swarm (beat-2, inn-cellar-adjacent; the entity placement lives in skeleton_scene.json). CANON-PLAUSIBLE, wiki.wanderinginn.com/Magical_Rats: 'Magical Rats' are rodents drawn to ambient/leaking magic ('any place with magic'), display diverse powers incl. fire breath -- the anchor-stone's residual rift-link leaking mana into the cellar is exactly the draw the wiki describes, so this is a direct thematic fit realized generic-diegetically (no single named subspecies is attested for a plain magic-drawn rat swarm). Two melee twins (rift_vermin_a/b, letter-suffix convention per training_dummy_a/b) + one ranged 'ember-touched' caster (rift_vermin_c, EXISTING flame_bolt skill -- the canon fire-breath power, no new skill.json entry). SPRITE STAND-IN: reuses `bat` (same convention as cave_spider/sewer_vermin, VISUAL-LOG flagged for a real rodent sheet). Given DISTINCT ids rather than repeating one id 2-3x in an encounter's `enemies` array -- a duplicate-id roster now fields every listed combatant correctly (WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id entries with a runtime suffix), but hand-authored distinct ids stay the clearer convention for a new multi-enemy roster: no suffix ever shows up in an event/snapshot id stream, and each individual can carry its own kit (rift_vermin_c's flame_bolt) without a shared-template constraint. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd RUIN_CELLS, GATED 0.55-0.95 at the warrior5_mage5 (~L10, 'L8-12 kit') representative build.

Rift_vermin_leak's second melee twin -- see rift_vermin_a's _comment for the full canon cite + distinct-id rationale. Identical stat template (a matched pair), given its own id per that convention (not required for a correct fielding anymore, but keeps ids suffix-free and each individual independently reskinnable).

Rift_vermin_leak's ranged member -- the canon 'fire breath' power (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Magical_Rats) realized via the EXISTING `flame_bolt` skill (goblin_shaman's spell_damage/range-4 bolt, no new skill.json entry -- flame is flame regardless of caster). `ai: ranged` so combat_ai.gd's ranged profile actually fires it (see wi-adding-an-encounter's autoplay gotcha: a melee-profile combatant never casts).

Ruin_guardian -- the anchor-stone pedestal's warden (beat-3 recovery run; the entity lives in ruin_surface, the pedestal gate is wired separately). CANON-CITE, wiki.wanderinginn.com/Chapter_3.07_H (+ wiki.wanderinginn.com/Thresk): the Ruins of Albez house a guardian construct/Golem the Horns of Hammerad fought at Warmage Thresk's treasury door -- 'a White-Hot Flame Golem', humanoid, animate flame with a mana-stone core, immensely dangerous at Horns' (much higher) power level. THIS combatant is NOT that same already-narratively-resolved construct (it was destroyed on-page; reusing it verbatim would also be far too strong for a ~L10 recovery-run gate) -- it's CANON-PLAUSIBLE: Albez is described as 'a breeding ground for Monsters' riddled with 'several dungeons' on a leyline, so a lesser ward-construct of the same animate-guardian family, sentineling a DIFFERENT anchor-stone pedestal elsewhere in the ruins, is a direct, non-colliding extrapolation of the same lore (construct/undead-class per the plan brief -- realized construct-side, no new mechanic). `ai: melee` (no new skill needed -- `tough_body`, an EXISTING skill, supplies the construct's durability flavor as flat +10 hp). SPRITE STAND-IN: `training_dummy` (an already-animate humanoid-shaped combat prop reads as a plausible guardian effigy without colliding with any established character's sprite -- reusing raskghar_awakened's or a goblin's sprite here was explicitly avoided per CLAUDE.md's stray-sprite-reuse gotcha). combat_scale looms it slightly above the escort wards. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd RUIN_CELLS, adjudicated win_lo/win_hi like deep_descent's raskghar_awakened (Relc-escorted cell explicitly banded, solo cell measured-only hard-mode frontier).

Ruin_guardian's first escort ward -- see ruin_guardian's _comment for the full canon cite. A lesser attendant construct (deep_warren boss+2-scouts structure precedent), given its OWN id (not repeated) per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.
Ruin_guardian's second escort ward -- identical template to ruin_ward_a (a matched pair), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.

Briar collector, `briar_collectors` encounter roster (the hollow's shallow wave). Canon-cite: wiki.wanderinginn.com/Plants -- Birevine ('vines stronger than steel rope, covered in razor-sharp thorns'); this roster is the witch's craft animating that plant into a debt-collecting construct, not an invented species. High con/moderate str (woody, grabs and squeezes), low dex (rooted, doesn't dodge) and minimal int/wis/cha (mindless while animate). No skills -- a plain thorn-lash `attack()`, escalation is `briar_collector_deep`'s job. Own sprite (`briar_collector`, plant-flavored) rather than a cross-species reuse.

Briar_collectors' second member -- see briar_collector_a's _comment for the full canon cite. Identical stat template (a matched pair, same convention as rift_vermin_a/b), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented there.

Deep briar collector, `briar_collectors_deep` encounter roster (the escalated second wave of the same hollow fight, arena `witch_hollow` shared with `briar_collectors` -- same canon-cite as briar_collector_a). Tougher template: higher con/str and `power_strike` (a heavier constricting grab, the EXISTING skill goblin_chieftain already uses -- no new skill.json entry) so the wave reads as a genuine step up rather than a reskinned repeat. Own sprite (`briar_collector_deep`, deliberately darker/taller) carries the escalation visually too.

Briar_collectors_deep's second member -- see briar_collector_deep_a's _comment for the canon cite + escalation rationale. Plain (no power_strike, slightly higher con instead) so the wave isn't two simultaneous 2x-multiplier hitters -- one heavy striker plus one bulkier grappler, same asymmetric-pair shape as goblin_ambush's raider+shaman. Given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.

River wolf, `river_wolf_pack` roster (arena `village_edge_night`, spawns only under the night phase gate -- unreachable at day by design). Canon-cite: wiki.wanderinginn.com/Monsters -- Wilwolf (an attested wild-wolf monster whose fur is harvested as a crafting material, i.e. ordinary huntable wildlife, not the goblin-tamed Carn Wolf subspecies). Faster/leaner than the briar collectors (higher dex, lower con) -- a pack hunter that closes quickly rather than a rooted grappler. No skills; river_wolf_c (the pack's alpha) carries the roster's only power_strike.

River_wolf_pack's second member -- see river_wolf_a's _comment for the canon cite. Identical stat template (a matched pack pair), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.

River_wolf_pack's third member, the pack's alpha -- see river_wolf_a's _comment for the canon cite. Slightly higher stats across the board plus `power_strike` (the pack leader's harder bite) so a 3-wolf night ambush has real teeth without every wolf carrying the same multiplier hit.
